stem: A pre-use check finds a missing machine guard. What is the best response?

stimulus.alt: Operator-care versus servicing boundary diagram separating assigned routine cleaning and external checks from guard removal, disassembly, jam clearing, electrical access, and other protected servicing work.
stimulus.caption: Use the operator-care boundary to decide whether the failed safeguard can be compensated for by routine work behavior.

choices: Use the equipment at reduced speed while keeping clear of the exposed moving part.
Increase distance from the machine and limit use to experienced operators until the guard is replaced.
Have a coworker watch the unguarded area while the equipment is used for essential work.
Do not use the equipment; follow the out-of-service and escalation procedure until the safeguard is properly restored.
rationale: A missing guard means a required safeguard is absent. Careful behavior, distance, experience, or a spotter do not replace the protection the guard provides. The machine should be removed from use according to procedure and escalated for authorized repair before operation resumes.
